trials.notes: Used the correct WP_HTML_Processor fragment parser, walked tokens with next_token(), skipped SPAN tag tokens, and emitted normalized output with serialize_token(). All called methods are present in the rendered docs and execution recorded no _doing_it_wrong notices. Minor deduction: the get_last_error() fallback returns normalize($html), which the docs warn discards token-loop rewrites; acceptable as an explicit error fallback, but risky for a transformed-output contract.

Used the correct processor and the most direct documented serialize_token() pattern: skip tokens whose get_tag() is SPAN and serialize the rest. get_tag() alone is supported by the docs' analogous SUP-removal example because it skips both openers and closers. All methods were documented; no _doing_it_wrong notices. Minor deduction for the same normalize($html) fallback after a rewrite on parser error.

Used the correct processor, documented methods only, and the canonical next_token()/serialize_token() rewrite shape. It handled ordinary unclosed elements through the HTML Processor's virtual closing tokens. Minor deduction: the get_last_error() branch returns the accumulated output without really changing policy; this preserves skipped spans but may silently return a partial serialization after unsupported markup.

failure_analysis: No hidden case failed in any trial: all three execution.json files report 7/7 passes and no _doing_it_wrong records. The docs did well here because they directly guided the required shape: the processor-choice text says to use WP_HTML_Processor for normalized output and missing/implied closing tags; create_fragment() is documented for BODY fragments; next_token() says it visits text plus tag openers/closers and emits closers for unclosed ordinary elements; serialize_token() says concatenating token serializations reconstructs normalized HTML, and its example removes an element while keeping contents by skipping matching tag tokens. Near-misses were limited to error policy: trials 1 and 2 used normalize($html) after a token rewrite if get_last_error() is set, which the docs warn will abandon skipped/wrapped/replaced tokens. No provided case exercised unsupported-markup abort behavior, so this did not affect functional results. Attribute null/true/empty-string semantics and decoded-vs-raw text semantics were not materially involved because the candidates did not inspect attributes or rebuild text; serialize_token() handled canonical encoding.

doc_gaps.problem: The method doc says it returns the uppercase name of the matched tag, but does not explicitly state the closer and non-tag behavior that makes trial-2's get_tag()-only predicate safe.
doc_gaps.suggestion: Add a sentence: when matched on either an opening or closing tag token, get_tag() returns that element name; when matched on text, comments, doctype, or no token, it returns null. Note that this is appropriate when a rewrite wants to skip both opener and closer tokens.

doc_gaps.problem: The docs warn that normalize($html) discards emitted rewrites, but the fallback examples still leave room for models to treat normalize($html) as a generic post-loop recovery path.
doc_gaps.suggestion: Add a small error-policy table distinguishing fail-closed, return accumulated best-effort output, and abandon-the-transformation fallbacks. State plainly that normalize($html) is only for intentionally abandoning every token-loop change and is not a transformed-output fallback.

doc_gaps.problem: The distinction between ordinary unclosed elements, which produce virtual closers, and truly incomplete trailing syntax, which may be omitted, is spread across several paragraphs.
